summary: Penghao Sun works in tibetology and history and archaeology. Between approximately 2017 and 2023, Sun conducted doctoral studies under supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp alongside committee members Janet Gyatso, Christopher P. Atwood, and Matthew King, among numerous other teachers.

Pentti Aalto (1917–1998) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki from circa 1935 to 1949 and later held a post there from circa 1958 to 1980.

Per Kjeld Sørensen (born 1950) is a scholar of tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Erik Haarh at the University of Copenhagen until circa 1980, later lecturing there (circa 1981–1989) before holding posts at Bonn (1991–1992) and Leipzig (1995).

Per Kvaerne (born 1945) specializes in tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning his Ph.D. at the University of Oslo (circa 1970–1973), he held posts there from circa 1975 to 2007 and at NIAS (1989–1991).

Perry Link (born 1944) works in sinology and linguistics. He studied at Harvard University from circa 1962 to 1976 and held academic posts at Princeton University (circa 1989–2008) and the University of California, Riverside (circa 2008).

Perry Schmidt-Leukel (born 1954) is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at LMU Munich (~1988–1998), Innsbruck (~1993–1997), Salzburg (~1998–2000), Glasgow (~1999–2009), and Münster (~2009–2020).

Peter Alan Roberts is a scholar in tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies under supervisors Michael Aris (circa 1995–1999) and Richard Gombrich (circa 1995–2001), also studying under Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979, among other teachers.

Peter Bisschop is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Groningen (~2000–2004) under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson. He held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford (2004–2005), Edinburgh (2005–2010), and Leiden (2010).

Peter Connolly works in religious studies and Indology. He completed his BA, MA, and Ph.D. at Lancaster University and was appointed Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester in 1980.

Peter D. Hershock works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Yale University and under traditional teachers Seungsahn and Ji Kwang Dae Poep Sa Nim, later serving as Director of the Asian Studies Development Program at the East-West Center.
Peter Ebbatson is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Oxford, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Walpola Rahula.

Peter Fenner specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under advisers Noble Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch until circa 1983, along with traditional teachers, and later held a post at Deakin University.

Peter Gaeffke (1927–2005) was an Indologist and linguist. During his academic career, he held posts at Utrecht University from circa 1968 to 1975 and as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1975 to 2004.

Peter Gyallay-Pap works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the London School of Economics and Political Science in 1990 and held an adjunct post at Adams State University.

Peter Harvey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He held a post at the University of Sunderland from circa 1976 to 2011, ultimately becoming Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies, and founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996.
Peter Haskel works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his graduate studies at Columbia University by circa 1988, having studied under Yoshito S. Hakeda until circa 1983.

Peter James Gilks works in Buddhist studies and tibetology. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and completed his PhD at the Australian National University (~2004–2010) under doctoral supervisor John Powers, alongside several traditional teachers.

Peter Koret is a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics. He completed his doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London around 1994 and held academic posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

Peter M. Scharf (born 1957) is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1983 to 1990, completing his dissertation under doctoral supervisor George Cardona (circa 1984–1990) and teacher Ludo Rocher.
Peter Masefield is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his studies under the supervision of Ninian Smart (circa 1974–1978) and L. P. N. Perera.
